{"title":"Punch the Dummy: Target Practice","mechanics":{"text":"Core loop: the player character stands within melee range of a single stationary target dummy and performs a punch action on player input (default binding: left mouse button or a designated 'Attack' button, e.g. E on keyboard / West face button on gamepad). Hit detection is resolved once per punch swing: a short-range forward hitbox/raycast is checked against the dummy's collider during the active frames of the punch animation. If the check registers contact with the dummy, exactly one 'hit' event fires: (1) a punch/impact sound effect plays, and (2) an on-screen hit counter increments by one. If the punch animation plays but does not connect with the dummy (player out of range or facing away), no sound plays and the counter does not increment. The dummy is immobile, has no health value, cannot be destroyed, and does not react beyond being the passive target of hit checks — it never resets, depletes, or triggers any secondary state. The counter is a simple persistent on-screen numeric display (e.g. 'Hits: 0') that only ever increases across the session; it is not a score, timer, combo multiplier, or damage value, and has no upper limit or reset condition. Input is rate-limited only by the natural duration of the punch animation (i.e., the player cannot start a new punch until the current animation finishes), preventing overlapping hit registrations from a single button press but adding no cooldown, combo, or stamina system beyond this animation-locking behavior.","assumptions":["Single player character controllable via standard movement (walk/run) plus one dedicated punch input; no additional attack types are added.","Punch input default: left mouse click (PC) or a single mapped gamepad button; rebinding is out of scope unless requested later.","One dummy exists in the scene at a fixed position and orientation; it does not move, rotate, or respawn.","Hit detection uses a simple forward hitbox or short raycast from the player's fist/hand bone active only during the punch animation's strike frames.","Exactly one hit-and-counter increment can occur per completed punch animation cycle, even if the hitbox theoretically overlaps the dummy for multiple frames.","The punch/hit sound is a single audio clip with no variation, layering, or randomization requested.","The on-screen counter is a plain numeric text UI element with no styling, animation, or visual feedback beyond updating the number.","No cooldown, stamina, or resource system limits punching beyond the animation's own playback duration."],"unresolved":[]},"theme":{"text":"Minimal training/practice setting with no narrative framing.
